name: fleet_haiku_macro_sector_rotation
strategy: Rate-hike acceleration with energy and financial leadership, earnings capture, and inflation hedge via crypto
reassessment_note: Fed's Sept 16 rate hike to 3.75%-4% with signals of continued tightening validates the rate-acceleration macro thesis. However, the book underperformed by 355bp (down 1.83% vs SPY +1.71%) due to over-defensive positioning. Energy sector (43% YTD, 27-52% commodity inflation) is leading beneficiary of rate hikes, while financials benefit from steeper yield curve expansion. Meanwhile, corporate earnings show 39.7% upward revisions with strong margins, rewarding cyclical exposure. Previous portfolio's emphasis on defensive healthcare (XLV +0.37%) and excessive cash (26%) missed cyclical opportunities. Rebalancing to capture energy leadership, financial yield benefits, and broad earnings strength while maintaining inflation hedge via Bitcoin and reducing cash drag from 26% to 15%.

positions.thesis: Energy is the primary beneficiary of Fed rate hiking cycle with oil prices surging 27-52% YoY from geopolitical tensions and supply constraints. XLE up 43% YTD; current entry (64.31) remains attractive with structural tailwinds from rate cycle favoring capital expenditure in exploration and production. Energy valuations supported by inflation in commodities and financial sector capital deployment.

Financials capture direct benefit of higher rates and steeper yield curve expansion. Fed now hiking with signals of continued tightening supports net interest margin expansion and improved capital markets activity (M&A, capital raising). Banks show upward earnings revisions; dividend yields (2-3%) supported by asset growth and rate-driven profitability.

Broad market exposure captures earnings growth engine: 39.7% upward revisions, strong corporate margins, AI infrastructure spending, and resilient employment (162k adds, wages outpacing inflation). Earnings provide fundamental support while rates rise, diversifying portfolio beyond rate-beneficiaries into profit-driven cyclicals and secular growth.

Bitcoin hedge against inflation persistence (3.4% August CPI, energy prices structurally elevated). Up 26% since book entry with strong institutional inflows ($3.5B+ ETF flows in August). Provides diversification from traditional equity rate-beneficiaries while capturing alternative asset class momentum. Scarcity value supports positioning in higher-for-longer rate regime.

Industrials leverage cyclical profit growth from AI data center capital spending and infrastructure investment. Upward earnings revisions expected from tech buildout; strong employment supports industrial capex. Small tactical allocation complements energy and financial rate-cycle thesis with exposure to capital-intensive business strength.

Materials provides marginal cyclical diversification to energy and industrials with exposure to semiconductor and electronic components profit growth from AI spending. Minimal tactical position supports primary energy/financial rate-hike thesis.
